baseline.inspection: All four package files read. Scoped git status, diff and cached diff were empty at assignment. No nested AGENTS.md found.

findings.finding: Detection, enforced unhealthy state and actual new host selection were not distinguished sufficiently. Panic was mentioned generically but the reference gave no concrete route from enforced ejection to continued selections.
findings.evidence: Envoy 1.35.0 outlier.rst states an ejected host remains unhealthy and may be selected during panic. hostSourceToUse increments lb_healthy_panic before either returning AllHosts or no host.
findings.consequence: An observer may mistake continued traffic for failed enforcement or early unejection, increasing duration or detector enforcement without changing the actual host-selection branch.
findings.resolution: Short core guard and focused conditional reference: correlate observing proxy, cluster, current health flags, panic counter deltas and new selection events; distinguish previous in-flight completion and other routing paths.

findings.finding: The generic fail-open/fail-closed advice did not explain the distinct effects of disabling panic versus failing traffic during panic.
findings.evidence: Versioned panic documentation, CommonLbConfig API and host-selection implementation distinguish normal health-based selection with threshold zero from no host selection in a panic priority with fail_traffic_on_panic enabled; priorities and runtime configuration affect panic eligibility.
findings.consequence: A response can propose blanket rejection even when retaining a healthy subset would meet the contract, or infer panic from a low fraction in one priority despite sufficient availability across priorities.
findings.resolution: Explain the two policy choices and capacity costs, keep adequate fail-open unchanged, qualify priority availability, and extend applicable drills with some-available and no-available-host cases.

changes.detail: Replaced the detection/removal wording with detection, enforced unhealthy state and actual new selections, retaining active-health recovery caveat.

Added one routed subsection on enforced ejection plus panic selection, runtime/priority conditions, evidence provenance, distinct policy choices, three versioned primary links and a focused extension to existing ejection drills.

Correlated failure, cap limitations, fail-open/closed contracts, draining and open/closed workload model controls.

+### When an enforced ejection still receives new selections
+
+An ejected host remains a cluster member marked unhealthy. In Envoy 1.35.0, round-robin and
+least-request can select it through **fail-open panic**, without an unejection. Inspect the
+effective policy, runtime override of `healthy_panic_threshold` (default 50%), and availability
+across priorities. When normalized total availability is 100%, sufficient capacity in other
+priorities prevents panic; a low healthy fraction in one priority alone is not proof of panic.
+Below that total availability, a priority below its panic threshold may use all its hosts.
+
+Correlate the observing proxy/cluster, current host flags, `lb_healthy_panic` counter deltas and
+actual upstream selections in the same window. The counter can increase in both fail-open and
+fail-closed panic; it does not prove an unhealthy host received work. Distinguish a **new
+attempt's selection** from completion of work selected before ejection or an existing stream.
+Traffic through another proxy, route or cluster does not establish this proxy ignored its state.
+
+If panic explains the new selections, increasing ejection duration does not change the selection
+rule. Retain fail-open when degraded attempts satisfy the service's contract. Otherwise compare
+`healthy_panic_threshold: 0`, which disables panic and retains normal health-based selection,
+with the applicable policy's `fail_traffic_on_panic: true`, which selects no host from a priority
+in panic even when some hosts remain available. In the legacy cluster API the latter is under
+`common_lb_config.zone_aware_lb_config`; verify the deployed policy's configuration surface.
+Disabling panic can concentrate load on survivors; failing traffic on panic sacrifices those
+remaining attempts. Neither creates capacity, and zero available hosts still requires an
+explicit rejection/fallback contract. Confirm the chosen behavior with actual destinations and
+request outcomes before claiming exclusion or availability.
